resources.string: Freeze the screen, crop any rectangle, then copy it, save it, or both.
Required — the selection is drawn in a window above everything else.
Off — capture will ask for recording permission each time.

ScreenClip works without this. Every capture just asks for recording permission first — Android requires that prompt every single time and no app can skip it. Turning this on lets ScreenClip take the shot directly, so there is no prompt at all.\n\nIt is an accessibility service, so Android will show a strong warning when you enable it. ScreenClip uses it only to take the screenshot you asked for.
You can come back here any time: long-press the app icon, or long-press the Quick Settings tile.

Find ScreenClip in the list and turn it on. If the switch is greyed out, go to Settings › Apps › ScreenClip › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings — that menu item only appears after you have tapped the greyed-out switch once.

Android has no way to ask whether the tile is currently in your Quick Settings, so these are two separate buttons rather than one switch. Removing hides it from Quick Settings and from the tile picker.
Instant capture off — captures will ask for permission again
Add it by hand: pull down Quick Settings, tap edit, drag ScreenClip in.
Lets ScreenClip capture the screen without a permission prompt every time.

ScreenClip uses this only to take the screenshot you asked for, and to notice when the Quick Settings panel has finished closing so it is not captured by mistake. It does not read screen content and does not run in the background.
